summary: Within an explicitly stated scale-indexed ODE schedule, finite accumulated strain and a scale-uniform forcing bound at the selected derivative order cannot produce divergence of that derivative norm through multiplicative frequency transport or direct high-frequency injection. Exact recurrence iteration gives a uniform norm bound, while geometric and polynomial exponent audits produce incompatible growth and forcing inequalities. This is a bounded obstruction for the schedule model, not a Navier--Stokes regularity or breakdown result.

value_assessment.novelty: The prior context treated fixed-amplitude integrability and localized residual formulas; this attempt separately audits an accumulating, scale-indexed correction schedule and identifies the precise escape conditions required to evade its bound.
value_assessment.evidence: DERIVATION.md gives the exact recurrence iteration, frequency-product estimate, direct-injection bound, and the geometric and polynomial exponent inequalities. verify_schedule.ps1 enumerates 66,048 geometric and 115,136 polynomial tuples with no matching-order witness, while a weakened-order positive control finds 27,209 feasible tuples.
value_assessment.falsifier: An explicit sequence satisfying finite total interval length, summable absolute strain, and a scale-uniform matching-order forcing bound while violating the derived recurrence, frequency, or injection bound would falsify the corresponding claim. A derivation error in the displayed finite algebra or a contradictory exact enumeration would also falsify it.

claims.statement: For the audited recurrence X_(n+1) <= exp(c_s e_n)(X_n + C_s d_n), finite sums of d_n and e_n and finite constants c_s and C_s imply a uniform bound X_n <= exp(c_s sum_j e_j)(X_0 + C_s sum_j d_j).
claims.evidence_summary: DERIVATION.md obtains the estimate by exact finite iteration, or equivalently by dividing by the accumulated exponential factor, and then bounds every remaining positive term by the total interval length.
claims.verification_method: Induct on n in the displayed recurrence, expand the product factors exactly, and bound each partial strain and duration sum by its stated finite total. A counterexample sequence under the same hypotheses would refute the claim.

claims.statement: For multiplicative frequency transport K_(n+1)=exp(sigma_n)K_n with |sigma_n|<=e_n, summable absolute strain prevents K_n from tending to infinity.
claims.evidence_summary: Taking logarithms gives |log(K_n/K_0)| <= sum_(j<n)e_j, so every transported frequency remains between two finite positive bounds whenever the absolute strain exposure is summable.
claims.verification_method: Multiply the finite recurrence, take logarithms, apply the triangle inequality, and compare the resulting partial sum with the assumed convergent series of absolute strain exposures.

claims.statement: For direct injections a_n=integral_(I_n) g_n dt with a scale-uniform matching-order bound K_n^s|g_n(t)|<=C_s, finite total interval length implies sum_n |a_n|K_n^s <= C_s T; the corresponding geometric and polynomial growth and forcing inequalities are incompatible under finite-time accumulation.
claims.evidence_summary: DERIVATION.md proves the integral bound and subtracts the geometric and polynomial exponent inequalities. verify_schedule.ps1 corroborates the bounded boxes with zero matching-order witnesses and a nonempty weakened-order positive control.
claims.verification_method: Apply the triangle inequality to each time integral and sum over disjoint intervals. For the exponent models, independently substitute the schedules into the norm-growth and forcing conditions and subtract the resulting inequalities; rerun verify_schedule.ps1 as a bounded corroborative check.

limitations: The audited recurrence is an abstract ODE schedule and has not been derived as a closure theorem for Navier--Stokes or for the compact-localization construction in the prior context.
The obstruction assumes derivative-norm amplification is charged to the stated strain exposure and that forcing has a scale-uniform seminorm at the same derivative order.
A nonlinear scale-transfer mechanism outside the recurrence, or a projection estimate without a scale-uniform matching-order constant, is not excluded.
The finite enumeration is corroborative only and covers the printed parameter grids; the universal statements rely on the analytical inequalities rather than the search.
failed_approaches: Pure multiplicative frequency transport does not create unbounded frequency when total absolute strain exposure is summable.
Fresh high-frequency injection does not create divergence in the selected derivative norm when matching-order projected forcing is uniformly bounded over intervals of finite total length.
next_actions: Derive or disprove a scale-uniform recurrence of the audited form from the compact-localization residual, with explicit dependence of the transport and forcing constants on anisotropic support scales.

proposed_tasks.title: Bridge the schedule obstruction to the localized PDE residual
proposed_tasks.objective: Starting from the existing compact-localization residual formulas, derive a fixed-order estimate for one correction interval that either has the audited recurrence form or exhibits a specific nonlinear transfer term outside it. Track every constant against the anisotropic support scales.
proposed_tasks.rationale: The bounded schedule obstruction is exact, but its relevance to Navier--Stokes depends on whether the localized PDE construction satisfies the same scale-uniform transport and forcing estimates.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: Produce a checkable interval estimate with explicit scale exponents and show that its constants are uniform across the accumulating schedule, or isolate one explicit term that prevents such uniformity.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: Identify the first residual or commutator term whose scale dependence cannot be bounded in the required norm, including the exact exponent mismatch and the assumption that fails.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Audit the derivation line by line against the recorded residual formulas, test dimensional and support-scale consistency, and verify representative exponent substitutions with exact symbolic or rational arithmetic.
